outputs.name: topk_distances
outputs.basis: verify.py's check |g - e| <= 1e-4 (1 + |e|) between the sorted reported top-k distances and the k smallest CPU distances (level1/nearest_neighbor/verify.py:43), here on the binary's float values (cuda/nn_cuda.cu, records[i].distance after the ROI, sorted) instead of the printed %f text; tol minus the B200 values' own deviation

outputs.name: topk_records
outputs.basis: the k reported records (cuda/nn_cuda.cu, records[i].recString after the ROI, the 48 characters printed before " --> Distance="), sorted bytewise, byte-identical. Exact is sound only because the registered queries have no tie at the k-th distance (verify.py fails a query whose k-th and (k+1)-th distances are within 2x the tolerance: cane4-k5 0.608 / 0.707; cane4-all reports every record), so every correct implementation reports the same set; verify.py checks that the set is a k-nearest set of db records (level1/nearest_neighbor/verify.py)

outputs.name: topk_record_distances
outputs.basis: the distance reported with each record of topk_records (records[i].distance, same order), within verify.py's |g - e| <= 1e-4 (1 + |e|) of that record's own CPU distance (the pairing record <-> distance); tol minus the B200 values' own deviation
